predicates.definition: The duty is stated by a current effective accepted unsuperseded normative source, not historical context, evidence, metadata, an exclusion, or a future proposal.
The duty bearer is explicitly linked to SPEC-0001's Linux operator, module, or production-host environment without inferring deployment lifecycle ownership.
The duty explicitly targets the same physical Stream Deck MK.2 rather than virtual buttons, emulator UI, generic Companion, or generic hardware.
The duty begins after login when the physical MK.2 disconnects and returns or enters a new enumerated USB epoch.
The current law requires automatic recovery without an operator intervention; observed behavior, may-investigate language, and future Slice preconditions are insufficient.

Recovery ends only when a physical MK.2 key press causally traverses Companion and produces the authorized OverlayKit command; descriptor ownership, Opening, Ready, UI projection, or pixels alone are insufficient.
The law supplies an explicit finite maximum whose start is the physical trigger and whose observable end is restored physical command delivery.

chainInvariant: All seven predicates belong to one explicitly linked obligation identity with the same role, device, trigger, recovery duty, outcome, and timing domain; exclusions, contradictions, and cross-record Cartesian mixing make the chain ineligible.

outcomePolicy.invalidEvidence: Any subject, schema, source, canonicalization, or artifact failure produces no hypothesis outcome.
outcomePolicy.inconclusive: Any pending human review, ambiguity, omission, conflict, opaque source, unclassified clause, or unresolved link after valid source admission.
outcomePolicy.supported: Complete accepted coverage, zero unknowns, and at least one eligible seven-predicate chain.
outcomePolicy.refuted: Complete accepted coverage, zero unknowns, and zero eligible seven-predicate chains.
